office_does: The prosecuting attorney decides which crimes are charged and prioritized, offers diversion, handles the county's civil cases and advises the county commissioners.
race_blurb: Appointed Republican Prosecutor Preston McCollam, a 13-year prosecutor who took 50.6% in the primary, faces Danny Tarkenton, an independent Iraq War veteran admitted to the bar in 2025. They differ on experience, on enforcement versus restorative justice, and on a sales tax for a new regional justice center.

candidates.summary: Appointed Spokane County Prosecutor since 2025 and former chief criminal deputy, endorsed by the sheriff, police unions and every county prosecutor since 1969.
highlights: Would push to restore felony charges for some drug crimes and aggressively prosecute fentanyl traffickers [S3][S6]
Started the 'Step Forward' felony diversion program and backs therapeutic courts [S3][S8]
Supports a narrowly tailored sales tax for a regional justice center with treatment services [S6][S7]

safety.basis: Enforcement-led platform (felony drug charges, consequences for repeat offenders, law-enforcement partnership) that also expands diversion and therapeutic courts.

experience.basis: More than a decade as a prosecutor, chief criminal deputy from 2023 and appointed head of the office since 2025.

taxes.basis: Would support asking voters for a sales tax increase narrowly tailored to fund the public safety overhaul.

spending.basis: Backs a new regional justice center with medical, behavioral health and drug treatment, and argues for more attorney positions and higher pay.

candidates.summary: Independent attorney, Iraq War veteran and former deputy prosecutor admitted to the bar in 2025, running on restorative justice and reducing repeat offending.
highlights: Calls a retributive 'prosecute everything' approach harmful and would expand restorative justice and therapeutic courts [S9]
Says jail crowding can be eased by choosing more carefully which crimes to prosecute [S6]
Endorsed by Mayor Lisa Brown, the Spokane Regional Labor Council and Fuse Washington; listed by NO HATE in WA State as opposing I-1 and I-638 [S4][S10]

safety.basis: Repeatedly centers diversion, restorative justice, therapeutic courts and charging restraint over prosecution alone.

experience.basis: Licensed in 2025, never elected, argues an outsider is needed and that trial experience is not required for the role.

reform.basis: Runs as an independent against 'party machines' and says prosecutors serve communities, not political parties.
